name: MonarchAiAgentCard
title: AiAgentCard
wrapsNative: MonarchCard (androidx.compose.material3.Surface) with androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column and FlowRow, composing MonarchAiAgentAvatar and MonarchBadge
summary: What an AI agent is and what it may do: its name and role, a description, capabilities, the tools it can call, the data it can see and who owns it, with optional actions; a compact variant summarises it for lists.
whenToUse: On an agent's profile screen, in an agent directory, or in a picker where people choose which agent to work with and need to know what it can do and see before they trust it.
whenNotToUse: For the agent's face beside a message, use MonarchAiAgentAvatar. For a log of what the agent did, use MonarchAiActionLog.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiAgentCard(agent: MonarchAiAgentRef, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, image: Painter? = null, description: String? = null, capabilities: List<String> = emptyList(), tools: List<MonarchAiAgentTool> = emptyList(), dataAccess: List<String> = emptyList(), owner: String? = null, state: MonarchAiAgentState = MonarchAiAgentState.Idle, variant: MonarchAiAgentCardVariant = MonarchAiAgentCardVariant.Full, labels: MonarchAiAgentCardLabels = MonarchAiAgentCardLabels(), actions: (@Composable FlowRowScope.() -> Unit)? = null)
data class MonarchAiAgentTool(name: String, description: String? = null)

class MonarchAiAgentCardLabels(kind: String? = null, capabilities: String? = null, tools: String? = null, dataAccess: String? = null, owner: String? = null, toolCount: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: agent
options.description: The agent: name, role, codename and id. The name and role are written; the codename and id feed the avatar's initials and color.

options.name: image
options.description: The agent's picture, loaded by the app. null shows the avatar's initials.

options.name: description
options.description: One or two sentences on what the agent is for.

options.name: capabilities
options.description: Short capability phrases, shown as neutral badges, such as "Drafts replies".

options.name: tools
options.description: The tools the agent can call, each with what it does. The compact card shows only their count.

options.name: dataAccess
options.description: What data the agent can read, such as "Documents in this space". Full card only.

options.name: owner
options.description: Who owns or maintains the agent. Full card only.

options.name: state
options.description: What the agent is doing now, shown by the avatar's ring and read for a state other than idle.

options.name: variant
options.description: Every section and the actions, or the compact summary for lists and pickers.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "AI agent", the section headings, "Owner" and the tool count.

options.name: actions
options.description: Buttons at the end of the full card, such as "Start a chat". They wrap onto new lines. Not shown on the compact card.

states.name: full
states.description: A 40dp agent avatar, the name and the role line, the description, then the sections that have content: What it can do, Tools, Data it can see, Owner, and the actions.

states.name: compact
states.description: A 32dp avatar, the name, the role line and a tool count ("3 tools"), the description and the capability badges; no other section and no actions.

states.name: idle, working, waiting, error
states.description: The agent avatar's ring and badge; a state other than idle is read by TalkBack. The working ring stands still when animations are off.

states.name: no role
states.description: The role line is "AI agent" alone.

appearance: MonarchCard's surface fill, default border and corners. The name in the strong body style and default text color, the role line and tool count in muted caption text, section headings in the subtle text color and label style, capability badges in the neutral subtle tone. The same roles in dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: A product pattern, experimental until a Rook app adopts it, built only from Monarch parts. Names and parameters follow iOS (MonarchAiAgentCard, MonarchAiAgentTool, MonarchAiAgentCardVariant, MonarchAiAgentCardLabels); the Android card also takes image: Painter? because Monarch loads no images, and actions is a trailing FlowRowScope slot. The web's headingLevel, as, nameId and descriptionId exist for HTML structure and for the web AiAgentPicker; on Android the name and role line are one heading and a picker builds its own rows. The web's owner can be any node, such as an avatar with a name; here it is text, as on iOS. The description is text rather than any node.
accessibility: The name and the role line are one TalkBack element with the heading property, read as "Research agent, Analyst · AI agent"; the role line always says "AI agent".
Section headings (What it can do, Tools, Data it can see) are headings.
Each tool is one element read as its name and what it does, built by a tested pure function.
The owner is read as "Owner, Sam Rivera".
The avatar is decorative; it is read only for a state other than idle, such as "Error".
On the compact card the capability badges are a traversal group named "What it can do".
Actions stay separate buttons with their own 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: Sections with no content are left out; a card with only an agent shows the header alone.
A blank description, owner or tool description is treated as absent.
A long name or description wraps; nothing is cut at font scale 2.0.
The compact card ignores dataAccess, owner and actions, as on the web and iOS.

examples.title: Full card
A compact card for a picker
examples.code:
@OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class)
MonarchAiAgentCard(
    agent = MonarchAiAgentRef(name = "Triage agent", role = "Support"),
    description = "Sorts new tickets and drafts first replies.",
    capabilities = listOf("Drafts replies"),
    tools = listOf(MonarchAiAgentTool("Read tickets"), MonarchAiAgentTool("Write reply")),
    state = MonarchAiAgentState.Working,
    variant = MonarchAiAgentCardVariant.Compact,
)
